title: Respuesta a incidentes y forense
description: CompTIA's incident response phases in order, the order of volatility, and digital forensics terms.
rows: Build the plan, team, tools, communication paths, and training before an incident.
CompTIA lists seven phases; NIST SP 800-61 groups them differently. Use CompTIA's names on the exam.
Recognize that an event may be an incident through alerts, reports, or monitoring.
Detection is noticing; analysis is confirming.
Validate the incident, determine scope and severity, and prioritize.
Rule out false positives before acting.
Limit the spread and damage, for example by isolating hosts or segments.
If an infection is active and spreading, containment comes FIRST, before eradication.
Remove the cause: malware, attacker accounts, persistence, and the exploited weakness.
Removing malware without closing the entry point invites reinfection.
Restore systems to normal operation and monitor for recurrence.
Restore from known-good backups or images and validate before returning to production.
Post-incident review to improve the plan, controls, and training.
Held after recovery; feeds back into preparation.
Determining the underlying reason an incident happened.
Fixes the cause, not just the symptom; supports lessons learned.
Proactively searching for threats that evaded existing detections.
Starts from a hypothesis, not from an alert.
Discussion-based walkthrough of a scenario with key stakeholders.
No systems are touched; lowest cost and disruption.
Hands-on exercise that mimics a real incident to test people and tools.
More realistic than a tabletop, more effort to run.
2. Memory (RAM), routing and ARP tables, process table
Running state, network connections, and loaded malware.
Lost on shutdown, so capture memory before powering off.
3. Temporary file systems and swap/page file
Can be overwritten during normal operation.
Files, logs, and artifacts on local drives.
Image with a write blocker and hash the image.
Logs held on SIEMs and other systems.
Subject to retention and rotation limits.
Order to preserve all relevant data and suspend normal deletion and retention schedules.
Overrides the normal retention policy until released.
Documented record of who handled evidence, when, and why, from collection to court.
A gap in custody can make evidence inadmissible.
Collecting evidence in a forensically sound way, such as bit-for-bit images.
Hash before and after to prove integrity; follow the order of volatility.
Protecting evidence from alteration or loss once collected.
Work on copies, never the original.
Identifying, collecting, and producing electronically stored information for legal proceedings.
Driven by legal requests, often following a legal hold.
Documenting findings, methods, and timeline for stakeholders or court.
Must be repeatable and defensible, not just conclusions.
